decision.question: QA2 execution backend: in-process scheduler versus durable-execution engine
decision.recommendation: in-process scheduler (current AgentOS coordinator, ADR-0002); keep the durable engine as a provider-neutral migration option only after a measurable trigger and a vendor-specific qualification run
decision.sensitivity: 222 deterministic runs (22 per-dimension weight +-50% perturbations, 200 seeded random integer weight compositions); zero flips and zero ties

probes.A_unsafe_resume: REJECTED - an actual second effect and receipt were produced in the raw ledgers; FAIL regardless of weighted score
probes.B_incomparable: REJECTED as INCOMPARABLE/NO_DATA - the workload hash diverged from the frozen manifest
probes.C_blind_retry: REJECTED - raw retry records lacked reconciliation evidence; FAIL

decision.migration_trigger: revisit only when a production-like benchmark proves sustained demand beyond the current single-process envelope, an availability-domain requirement appears, or a new trust boundary is introduced; re-run this qualification against the selected vendor before migration
decision.non_goals: no production vendor installation, no production SLO or availability claim, no core runtime migration, and no re-decision of the S1-005 topology

limitations: Model-based comparison on a same-host research station: durable-engine costs combine S1-005 E1/E2 measurements with documented lease/visibility assumptions (100 ms lease timeout, 105 ms modeled recovery); no vendor engine was installed.
Low/nominal arrival rates link to the S1-002 planning envelope; the 20,000/s high load is an explicit simulator saturation probe, not a production profile.
Multi-host partition behaviour and vendor timer semantics are unknown and excluded from scoring.
Producer and verifier labels are process-separated roles in one local environment, not external human auditors.
Migration triggers remain design obligations until a production-like follow-up benchmark measures them.
note: research-plan PASS_WITH_LIMITS is a research evaluation; it never sets Goal ACCEPTED. Revision 5 supersedes revision 4 after R2 added raw-run authority, real commit/outbox/replay and checkpoint/fencing traces, open-loop saturation, exact provenance and dependency binding, behavioral probes, and deterministic S2 fault coverage.
